question.text: Under the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008, what must an intermediary do upon cancellation of its certificate of registration?

answer.text: Return the certificate to SEBI, cease registered activity, transfer activities or allow clients to withdraw/transfer securities and funds, make provisions for any liability incurred or assumed, and take required actions on records and investor money
Only make provisions for any liability incurred or assumed
Only return the certificate to SEBI and cease registered activity
Only transfer activities to another registered person and allow clients to withdraw securities/funds

explanation.text: The Logic: Upon cancellation of registration the intermediary must return the certificate, cease all registered activities, transfer activities to another registered person or allow clients to withdraw/transfer their securities and funds, make provisions for any liability incurred or assumed, and take the required actions in respect of records and investor money. The Trap: Each "Only..." option states a real post-cancellation obligation, but the regulations require the intermediary to do all of them together — picking one obligation alone is incomplete. Note: Cancellation does not end client-protection duties — the intermediary must still protect investor money and records and ensure orderly transfer of activity before exiting the regulated space.
